fact_previews: The Single Responsibility Principle (SRP) teaches how to design classes and components with a single, well-defined responsibility.
The Open-Closed Principle (OCP) focuses on designing code that is open for extension but closed for modification.
The Substitution Principle (LSP) helps in designing classes and interfaces that can be used interchangeably without affecting program correctness.
The Interface Segregation Principle (ISP) emphasizes defining small, focused interfaces to prevent clients from depending on unused methods.
The Dependency Inversion Principle (DIP) emphasizes decoupling high-level modules from low-level modules and relying on abstractions.
